title: Raga Suhi
hookLine: a raga of union and weddings that opens with a clean vessel, a pot of milk and a churn

lines: A POT LEFT FOR THE NIGHT.
A RAGA OF UNION OPENS IN A KITCHEN.
cards: A steel pot on the kitchen counter, a dish towel over the lid, left alone for the night. Warm milk went in, then a spoonful of yesterday's yogurt.
By morning the two have become one thing, thick and set, and nobody can pull them apart again. Punjabi kitchens know that pot, and so does the Guru Granth Sahib.
Today's raga is tied by tradition to weddings and union, and its very first hymn isn't about a bride at all. It's about the pot. Today: Raga Suhi.

teach.b: First, the setting. Suhi follows Tilang in the Granth's order, opening on ang seven twenty-eight.
Sikh tradition links it with union and weddings, and its pages hold songs of the bride and the beloved; tomorrow opens some of them. Second, the kitchen.

teach.h: WASH THE VESSEL, THEN FETCH THE MILK.
teach.b: Guru Nanak's opening hymn, in paraphrase: wash the vessel, sit down, purify it with incense, and only then go out for the milk. The milk is your deeds. Awareness is the culture you stir in.
And set it free of craving for a reward.
Third, the refrain: chant the one Name; every other work bears no fruit. Fourth, the churn.

teach.h: THE MIND AS THE CHURN'S HANDLES.
teach.b: Make this mind the handles, and staying awake the cord. Let the tongue repeat the Name, and churn like that: this is how the nectar is found.
Why would a raga of union begin here? Milk and culture become one only in a clean pot, left in peace, with nobody poking at it to see if it's ready.

The hymn describes union the way a cook does: prepare the vessel, bring something good, add a little of what's alive, and wait without grasping. Then the churning, the patient work that brings out what was hidden.
Some readers hear the soul and God becoming one. Others hear a plain daily discipline. Both start with the same instruction: wash the pot first.

how: Shabads from the Suhi section of the Guru Granth Sahib are sung in kirtan in Raga Suhi, and because Suhi holds the Lavan, the raga is heard at the Anand Karaj, the Sikh wedding.

a harvest song sung while churning the butter

games.q: inside Suhi's first hymn — tap the pairs.

s: the Suhi section opens with a hymn about a bride
it opens with Guru Nanak's hymn of a washed vessel, milk, culture and a churn.
the hymn says to set the milk while hoping for a reward
it says to set it free of craving for a reward.
the hymn's refrain is to chant the one Name
chant the one Name; every other work bears no fruit.

games.q: you're making yogurt the way the hymn describes. what comes first?
o: pour the milk into whatever pot is handy.
wash the vessel and purify it, then fetch the milk.
add extra culture so it sets faster.
games.why: wash the vessel, sit, give it incense, and only then go for the milk. the hymn starts with the heart that will hold it.

practice: If you'd like, play a shabad in Raga Suhi, or simply let the breath slow.

For a minute, wash the pot, letting go of whatever is still sloshing around from today, one thing at a time; then leave it be, without checking whether it's working, like milk left to set, with Waheguru as the one word you stir in if you pray, or the breath alone if you don't.

wordCard.voice: Raga Suhi. The raga after Tilang, linked by tradition with weddings and union, which opens with a clean vessel, milk, a little culture and a churn. Today's word.
